summary: I ran `taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean` on the file twice. It exits 0 with no messages (about 4 s wall, about 300% CPU). The olean (09:11:40) is newer than the source (09:11:35). The only occurrences of 'sorry' are two docstring mentions of Models' former tagged sorry. The sweep campaign/WP-35g/Axioms.lean covers all 147 declarations of the file, the same set I extracted myself. Re-run against the fresh olean, it gives propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound everywhere, propext/Quot.sound for isOpen_of_le_sptop, and no sorryAx. So the cited library results (GX.spread_top_deck, maxBranched_isGaloisian_cc, complete_path_carac, exists_homeomorph_maxBranched_qDisc, …) are genuinely proved. Name clashes: the 147 names compared against the 3,221 declared in GX/ and the other scaffold files (C locale) intersect in nothing. The dispatch's main item is DONE. The proof of lem:spread_top (paper l.2010–2061, not l.2068–2136 as the dispatch says, which REPORT correctly notes) is built end to end as GX.spread_top_of_local: all five clauses (a) FC + connected + LPC, (b), (c), (d), (e), under three added hypotheses, each reported. (1) N → M Galoisian, used only by (d) through the proof's γ̄ (l.2015), the dispatch's reading. (2) p⁻¹(R) connected, the proof's 'R̂ weakly connected' (l.2047). (3) StrongLocallyConnectedOrd, the Claim's 'we may assume Ô ∩ R̂ connected' (l.2029), proved EQUIVALENT to (c) (isPortly_strongPullTop_iff_local). This is not a hidden hypothesis carrying the conclusion. It is disclosed as equivalent to (c), and it is necessary in the presence of every other hypothesis. not_spreadTopGalConnCE (sector topology at the branch point of 𝔻_∞ → ℂ, q = id Galoisian, hRc proved) refutes '(c) ∨ (e)'. not_spreadTopGalLocalCE (half-cut plane, q = id, local hypothesis PROVED by strongLocallyConnectedOrd_halfCut via M̃^∅ ≅ ℂ) refutes connectedness. I also checked the converse directions: (e) ⇒ (c), and (a)+(b)+(c) ⇒ hRc. So spread_top_corrected together with spread_top_of_local is a characterization, the strongest true form DEC-27 asks for. SpreadTopPrinted, SpreadTopGalLocalCE and SpreadTopGalConnCE each carry exactly the hypotheses claimed, binder for binder: the printed statement, then everything but hRc, then everything but hH. None is vacuous. T = the natural topology satisfies every hypothesis of spread_top_of_local, and the two counterexamples instantiate all the others concretely. Fidelity: hSc is the library-wide presupposition of M̃^S (cf. DEC-70). N T2/LPC/FC is DEC-66(a). (b) is the induced-topology equality, (d) quantifies over deckGroup of M̃^S → M, (e) is IsBranchedCovering for (p^*T, T). def:topological_spaces_continuous_map is certified verbatim (GX.strongPullTop_eq_generateFrom_union, rfl after generateFrom_union), with p's continuity unused, and is legitimately marked. The three remarks stay partial, unmarked, each with a stated reason: rem:intuitively_spread_thinner_than is a reading of 'intuitively' with the literal claim refuted; rem:hypothesis_model_spaces_necessary needs the §4 BTZ tamifying topology, not in lean-gx; rem:quotient_virtually_tame adds 'M̃ → M Galoisian', now discharged from reg M slsc in M by the new GX.quotient_virtually_tame_cover_of_slsc, proved as spaces not as (G,X)-manifolds. All five ledger labels of l.1984–2162 have a REPORT row and appear within the first 4000 characters of the module docstring. Only def:topological_spaces_continuous_map is marked. No blocker or major. The minors below are bookkeeping and wording, several carried over from WP-27k AUDIT-2.

issues.where: spread_top_of_local / spread_top_corrected (d); REPORT lem:spread_top findings[6]; SCOPE (e)
issues.problem: The necessity of 'N → M Galoisian' for (d) is argued informally only: a non-normal 3-sheeted intermediate cover with trivial Γ(N/M), and T cut at one point of a fibre. I checked the sketch and it is sound: a deck transformation of M̃ sending a natural point over n₁ to a cut point over n₀ is not p^*T-continuous. Unlike the other two added hypotheses, it has no formal counterexample. It is disclosed, the dispatch prescribed the reading, and the paper's only application (V̂ → V) is Galoisian, so this is not a major.
issues.fix: Optional: formalize the cex (needs an explicit non-normal finite cover, heavy), or keep it as a recorded informal finding and ask the author.
